clue.text: American general means to raise child

parts.note: a jack is a device for lifting a car or other heavy load
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A US commander finds a way to bring up his offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: Stonewall Jackson was a Confederate general in the American Civil War.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas 'Stonewall' Jackson and Andrew Jackson were both celebrated generals of the United States.

clue.text: Artist gives writer a weapon to point

parts.note: Henry James was an American-born novelist
a gun is a weapon
N is north, a point of the compass

explanation.surface: A painter hands an author something to aim.
explanation.walkthrough: Sir James Gunn was a Scottish portrait painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir James Gunn painted portraits, including a state portrait of Queen Elizabeth II.

indicators.note: talked of means the word for crest is said aloud and we write a word sounding the same

parts.note: a cockscomb is the red crest on a cockerel's head

explanation.surface: A dandy, much gossiped about, gains a heraldic badge.
explanation.walkthrough: A coxcomb is a vain, showy man; the crest on a cock's head is pronounced the same.
explanation.definitionFit: A coxcomb is a conceited dandy, another word for a vain dressy man.

clue.text: In the same way, army is ill-organized

indicators.note: organized means the letters of army is ill are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A sickly army, equally badly run.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organized' rearranges ARMY IS ILL into the answer; 'ill-organized' looks like one adjective but splits.
explanation.definitionFit: Similarly means likewise, in a matching manner.

parts.note: the clue describes a musical key that is anything but E, which can be put as ..., run together into a word

explanation.surface: Every button on the keyboard but one.
explanation.walkthrough: A key here is a musical key, and E is one of them: any key except E is 'not E'. A note is also what any key of a piano sounds.
explanation.definitionFit: A musical key is named after a pitch, and each piano key sounds a single pitch.

explanation.surface: Someone babbles on about pastries.
explanation.definitionFit: To waffle is to ramble without saying much; waffles are also gridded batter cakes cooked in an iron.

parts.note: the clue reads as a sealant used aboard ship, but means the silicate solution once used to keep eggs, which also names a tumbler set on a table, the board

explanation.surface: Something that protects goods on a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'On board' suggests a ship; a board is also a dining table, where a drinking tumbler stands. Sodium silicate solution, the other sense, was used to keep eggs fresh.
explanation.definitionFit: Water glass is sodium silicate solution, formerly used to keep eggs from spoiling, and also a drinking tumbler at the table.

explanation.surface: The scope shown by a writer of music.
explanation.walkthrough: John Field was an Irish composer who invented the nocturne.
explanation.definitionFit: A field is an area or scope of activity; John Field was an Irish composer of piano nocturnes.

parts.note: the friend at court is a barrister, whom fellow counsel call my ... friend in court

explanation.surface: What kind of ally does one have among royalty?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Court' suggests a royal court; in an English law court one barrister refers to another as 'my learned friend'.
explanation.definitionFit: Barristers address each other in court with this adjective, meaning scholarly.

annotationWithheld.why: Poetic captain finds writer aboard ? (5): SPENS is PEN inside SS, and 'aboard' alone gives both SS and the container signal, one word doing two jobs

explanation.surface: The guiding rule of a gunslinger.
explanation.walkthrough: Hiram Maxim invented the first fully automatic machine gun, so he is the 'gun-man'.
explanation.definitionFit: A maxim is a short statement of a general rule; Sir Hiram Maxim gave his name to the Maxim machine gun.

parts.note: Emma is read not as a woman seen in person but as the title of Jane Austen's novel, printed on a leaf at the front of the book

explanation.surface: Where did we catch sight of Emma?
explanation.walkthrough: The clue pretends Emma is a person we glimpsed somewhere; she is the book, and the first thing one sees of a book is the sheet bearing its name.
explanation.definitionFit: The leaf at the front of a book shows its name, so a novel called Emma announces itself there.

clue.text: These reels can be put back in the vessels

indicators.note: put back tells us to write the boats' name from its end to its start

parts.note: sloops are small single-masted sailing boats

explanation.surface: Reels of film can be returned to their containers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be put back' turns SLOOPS, the vessels, round to give the reels.
explanation.definitionFit: Spools are cylinders on which thread, film or tape is wound, the same thing as reels.

indicators.note: including means the canvas shelters hold the word for free inside them

parts.note: tents are shelters put up for a short stay
to rid is to free of something

explanation.surface: A campsite that comes with planes thrown in for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' puts RID inside TENTS. The Trident was a British airliner of the 1960s.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hawker Siddeley Trident was a three-engined British passenger jet.

clue.text: Lover, of course — and hater, possibly

parts.note: the sweet is the dessert course of a meal

indicators.note: possibly means hater is one possible arrangement of the letters wanted

explanation.surface: A partner who might equally turn to loathing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Of course' looks like 'naturally'; here it is the pudding course, SWEET. 'possibly' rearranges HATER into HEART.
explanation.definitionFit: A sweetheart is a beloved, someone one is in love with.

indicators.note: headless means the word for figure loses its first letter

parts.note: a figure is a number, as in a sum

explanation.surface: A paint applied to a statue lacking its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'headless' takes N from the front of NUMBER. 'Figure' suggests a sculpture; here it is a numeral.
explanation.definitionFit: Umber is a natural brown earth pigment, and so a shade of brown.

clue.text: Document needs altering in Greater London

parts.note: a will is the legal document stating how an estate is shared

indicators.note: altering means the letters of needs are put in a different order

explanation.surface: A piece of paperwork must be amended somewhere in the capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'altering' rearranges NEEDS into ESDEN after WILL. The definition reads as 'a place in Greater London'.
explanation.definitionFit: Willesden is a district of north-west London, inside the Greater London area.

clue.text: Nettie ran trip to provide diversion

indicators.note: trip means the letters of nettie ran stumble into a new order

explanation.surface: Nettie organised an outing to amuse people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trip' rearranges NETTIE RAN; it looks like an excursion Nettie ran.
explanation.definitionFit: To entertain is to amuse, to give people a pleasant diversion.

clue.text: Of course poor Aunt is going to recover !

indicators.note: poor means the letters of aunt are in poor shape and reordered

parts.note: to rally is to recover strength after illness

explanation.surface: Naturally a sick aunt will get well again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'poor' rearranges AUNT into NATU, then RALLY follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Naturally is said to mean obviously, as expected.

parts.note: Young looks like a surname, but the clue means a husband and wife who are young in their marriage

explanation.surface: A couple called Young, addressed formally.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital Y makes Young look like a family name; read it as an adjective: a couple only just married.
explanation.definitionFit: A pair who have only recently married are fresh to wedded life, a new Mr and Mrs.

clue.text: Cut short holiday and let repair work finish

indicators.note: finish says the rearranged letters come at the end, after the holiday

parts.note: Whit is the Whitsun holiday, the week after Whit Sunday

indicators.note: repair work means the letters of let are mended into a new order

explanation.surface: A truncated break, with repairs to a rented property to complete.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repair work' rearranges LET into TLE, which 'finish' sends to the end after WHIT. Whitsun is the Christian festival of Pentecost, traditionally a British holiday.
explanation.definitionFit: To whittle down is to pare away gradually, reducing something in size.

explanation.surface: A warped bit of Victorian fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Twist is the orphan hero of Dickens's novel of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Oliver Twist is a character created by Charles Dickens; a twist is also a bending out of shape.

clue.text: I propose to go round Puerto Rico, to get better

indicators.note: to go round means the proposal phrase is wrapped around the island's abbreviation

parts.note: to move a motion at a meeting is to propose it, so I propose is I move

explanation.surface: A traveller plans a Caribbean tour to recover health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to go round' puts PR inside I MOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: To improve is to become better.

clue.text: Time for wit of a sort — frivolous

indicators.note: of a sort means the word wit is offered in another arrangement

parts.note: light reading or light-hearted talk is frivolous

explanation.surface: A moment for some kind of humour, not to be taken seriously.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of a sort' rearranges WIT into TWI, followed by LIGHT.
explanation.definitionFit: Twilight is the dim period after sunset, a time of day.

clue.text: Food for journey to Egyptian capital

parts.note: a trip is a journey

indicators.note: capital means the first, capital letter of Egyptian

explanation.surface: Provisions for a voyage to Cairo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Egyptian capital' looks like Cairo; it is the capital (first) letter of 'Egyptian'. Tripe is cow's stomach, a traditional British dish.
explanation.definitionFit: Tripe is the stomach lining of cattle, cooked and eaten.

parts.note: one is I, and the 's adds S
Sue is a short form of Susan, a girl's name

explanation.surface: Kids team up with a person's young daughter.
explanation.walkthrough: Issue is the legal word for offspring.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue means offspring, a person's descendants.

explanation.surface: A comic performer working in clothing.
explanation.walkthrough: Ruth Draper was a famous American performer of solo character sketches; 'the rag trade' is British slang for the clothing business.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruth Draper performed celebrated monologues; a draper sells cloth, so works in the textile and clothing business.

explanation.surface: A seasoned milliner.
explanation.walkthrough: Felt is the pressed woollen material many hats are made of.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is the past tense of feel, meaning underwent; felt cloth is used to make hats.

parts.note: unwillingly is read as without a will, and late as dead, describing someone who died leaving no will

explanation.surface: Someone arriving behind time against their wishes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Unwillingly' seems to mean reluctantly and 'late' tardy; read them as 'lacking a will' and 'deceased'.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who dies without having made a will is said to die in that legal condition.

parts.note: a bell's toll is its ring

explanation.surface: A circle formed by a reef.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the reef, and it is also A plus TOLL, the ringing of a bell.
explanation.definitionFit: An atoll is a ring-shaped reef or island of coral enclosing a lagoon.

clue.text: Always set out to get top place

parts.note: ever means always, as in for ever

indicators.note: out means the letters of set are put in disorder

explanation.surface: A determined climber always sets off to reach the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges SET into EST after EVER.
explanation.definitionFit: Mount Everest is the highest mountain on Earth, the top spot on the planet.

clue.text: Attempt to include girl in commercial undertaking

indicators.note: to include means the word for attempt holds the girl's name inside it

parts.note: a try is an attempt
Anne is a girl's name

explanation.surface: A bid to bring a young woman into a business venture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to include' puts ANNE inside TRY.
explanation.definitionFit: A tannery is a business where hides are turned into leather.
